title: RTP Stream Analysis: Process more streams than two, audio save removed
description:
Changes:
- Removed all old Save audio and Save payload code, same functionality
  is in RTP Player now
- Dialog shows multiple streams, each stream has own tab
- Tabs can be closed
- RTP Analysis Dialog is singleton as other VoIP dialogs.
- Implemented Set/Add/Remove actions from other dialogs

Side changes:
- Signals changed to plain calls in main_window. It was mixing calls for
same signal name and different dialogs
- added 3 new icon generators (circle, crosscheck, triangle)
  to ui/qt/utils/stock_icon.h

Can you revert all those strange new UI playlist changes? If you will press add (now "set playlist") two or 3 times, it will crash wireshark. Also it is very slow and I do not understand at all how to play anything now??

Also what does remove from playlist does on when you open? There is no playlist yet? How does it work?

Hi,
I'm not happy to hear that it is slower and crashing. My aim was to make it much faster and responsive than before and my tests shows it works that way. I'm now able to play high tens of streams without any delays as before.

I'm aware that change in UI is strong and I'm working on manual to describe it.

The general idea is to allow to analyse environment where hundred of streams must be analysed. In this case streams are coming from many different calls. Therefore now you can control player from anywhere:
- VoIP/SIP Calls
- Flow Sequence
- RTP Analysis
- RTP Streams

At each of this dialog, you can:
- set - clear playlist and add selected streams to player
- add - add selected streams to player
- remove - remove selected streams from player

Set is used when you would like to start with new analysis. Add is useful when you find next interesting call/stream. Remove is useful when you would like to remove e.g. all streams for SIP call from player because you know that this call is not interesting for you.

Then in player you can remove streams if you recognize they are useless for later analysis. With combining of add/remove from all tools mentioned above I'm now able to select list of streams I'm interested in analysis. It was not possible before.
BTW export works with multiple/all unmuted channels too.

In player you can select, deselect channels in play list and in waveform too. All selecting is useful for deleting, exporting, mute/unmute etc.

I hope that legacy procedure how to play stream is not changed. You click on stream or call and press Play/Set or Play/Add (yes, there is one more menu) and player is shown with the stream. Then you press Play icon and it plays.

Back to observed issues:
1) I'm working on building windows environment to catch issue with hanging play at the end of play you reported elsewhere.
2) Can you describe sequence how to crash wireshark? I'm not aware of it. I propose to create bug and put id there.
3) When you observing "slow" response? During decoding, during playing, ...? Can you provide sample.pcap and description of delay?
4) I hope I described changes above. I'm working on manual...

Feel free to comment new changes!

> Remove is useful when you would like to remove e.g. all streams for SIP call from player

An example: VLC. You can **get playlist** by pressing **Ctrl-L**. But there is **no way** to get playlist in Wireshark. Also for **no playlist** why removing stream is even available?

> Can you describe sequence how to crash wireshark?

Press "Set playlist" many times **fast**. Since it is not blocked on execution, it will crash wireshark as it will open many play windows. Also maybe you should rename Set playlist to just "play" or "play playlist" (at least I hope I understand you correctly).

Playlist means list of streams loaded into the player. Player window now can be opened on background and you can add/remove streams to it with other tools.
I was looking for better description for list of streams better than "list of streams in the player window" and I tried playlist. Can you propose something different and more clear?

I will check observed opening of player window multiple times. It should not be possible, thank you for reporting it.

@ValZapod
Opening of multiple player windows should be fixed by !2653 once merged.
Can you check and confirm that you are able to play audio (solved with !2641)?

You mentioned that it is "slow". Can you describe what behaves slow and compare it e.g. to 3.4 branch?

> and confirm that you are able to play audio

Nope, but it does not crash anything anymore.

> You mentioned that it is "slow".

What I meant is not the opening (it is almost the same) the play window. I meant the overall left and right channel desync problem (when you press on pause) and big latency on initial playing (which does not happen on pause and play).

"Nope" mean you hear no audio or it is delayed as described next to it?

There should be small delay after press of the play button which is indicated in text field below playlist as "Preparing to play", but then it should play with no delay.
Can you provide me with sample to test it?

> "Nope" mean you hear no audio

No audio. It also does not crush by the end.

> Can you provide me with sample to test it?

I test it all on that DTMF sample.

I see. No audio just on soundcard which was crashing before. Other soundcards works fine?

SIP_DTMF2.cap? But there is just a few clicks one channel and unaudible noise in second channel.
But I expect that e.g. https://wiki.wireshark.org/SampleCaptures?action=AttachFile&do=get&target=SIP_CALL_RTP_G711 
is unsynchronized too. Right?

> There should be small delay after press of the play button which is indicated in text field below playlist as "Preparing to play"

I have a fast enough PC so that is almost not visible. Indeed there is one like for 0.2 seconds. That has nothing to do with the delay after that. That delay also happens when you pause in the middle and will wait for at least 10 seconds and then restart! I you will not wait, the sound after pause is immediate.


> is unsynchronized too

That is hard to tell there, since there is just voice there and no white noise.

> Other soundcards works fine?

I will further test it for you.

commits_data.message:
RTP Stream Analysis: Process more streams than two, audio save removed

Changes:
- Removed all old Save audio and Save payload code, same functionality
  is in RTP Player now
- Dialog shows multiple streams, each stream has own tab
- Tabs can be closed
- RTP Analysis Dialog is singleton as other VoIP dialogs.
- Implemented Set/Add/Remove actions from other dialogs

Side changes:
- Signals changed to plain calls in main_window. It was mixing calls for
same signal name and different dialogs
- added 3 new icon generators (circle, crosscheck, triangle)
  to ui/qt/utils/stock_icon.h

commits_data.title: RTP Player: Added ability to save streams as .au and .wav
commits_data.message:
RTP Player: Added ability to save streams as .au and .wav

Features:
- saves multiple streams (all selected and unmuted)
- saves streams same way they are played (jitter buffer, sampling, ...)
- only streams with audio (play rate >0) are exported
  - streams with play rate == 0 are silently ignored even selected for
    export
- all exported streams must use same play rate (user can change it
  before save)
